name: M4 in Markdown (injection)
comment: Injected (not just included) so m4 constructs are recognized even in the middle of an already-open Markdown block (e.g. a multi-line paragraph or list item), not only at the start of a line. A plain 'include text.html.markdown' composition can't do that: once Markdown's own paragraph/list/etc. rule has started matching, only *its* nested patterns are considered for the rest of that block - see README.md. The '-comment -string' exclusions are load-bearing: an injection selector matches anywhere the root scope is on the scope stack, i.e. INCLUDING inside the regions this very grammar opens - without the exclusions, the <!-- comment rule fires inside the [[<!--]] string of the standard changecom preamble, and the [[ string rule fires inside comments, each preventing the other's end delimiter from ever matching and cascading to the end of the file. Comments take no nested highlighting at all, and strings handle their own nesting via their own patterns, so both are safe to exclude. Unlike the plain source.m4 grammar, this grammar deliberately does NOT assume m4's default delimiters: it hardcodes the README's recommended .md.m4 convention instead - [[...]] quotes (changequote([[,]])) and <!-- ... --> comments (changecom([[<!--]],[[-->]])). m4's default backtick quote and # comment are left entirely to Markdown, where they mean inline code and headings; a static grammar can only pick one set of delimiters, and for .md.m4 files the recommended convention is the right bet, not the m4 defaults (which cascade catastrophically against Markdown's backticks - see README). Files that DON'T follow the convention still get corrected by the language server, whose comment/string semantic tokens follow the live changequote/changecom state.

md-m4-comment.comment: The conventional .md.m4 comment delimiters (changecom([[<!--]],[[-->]])). Deliberately identical to Markdown's own HTML-comment syntax, so one wrapper hides text from the rendered output AND protects it from macro expansion. Correct even in files that never call changecom: an HTML comment is a comment to Markdown regardless.
md-m4-comment.name: comment.block.m4

md-m4-quoted-string.comment: The conventional .md.m4 quote delimiters (changequote([[,]])), with balanced nesting like any m4 quote pair. Doubled brackets are not meaningful CommonMark syntax (single [...] is link text), so this doesn't fight the Markdown grammar. Note for wiki-flavored Markdown users: [[wikilinks]] will render as m4 strings here - in this dialect that's what they are.
md-m4-quoted-string.name: string.quoted.other.m4

md-m4-code.comment: The delimiter-independent m4 rules, shared with source.m4, plus this dialect's own quote rule. Everything here is valid both at top level and inside a quoted string (a quoted string is usually a deferred macro body).
